origin.description: Create a function that signals progression conditions.
origin.usage: progressor(steps = length(along), along = NULL, offset = 0L, scale = 1L, transform = function(steps) scale * steps + offset, message = character(0L), label = NA_character_, trace = FALSE, initiate = TRUE, finalize = FALSE, auto_finish = TRUE, on_exit = !identical(envir, globalenv()), enable = getOption("progressr.enable", TRUE), envir = parent.frame())

arguments.name: steps
arguments.text: Number of steps. When omitted, steps is length(along). along = NULL gives length 0.

arguments.name: transform
arguments.text: Applied once at creation. The default is scale * steps + offset.

arguments.name: initiate
arguments.text: If TRUE, signal type initiate with steps and auto_finish when the progressor is created.

arguments.name: on_exit
arguments.text: If TRUE, signal type finish when the creating frame returns. TRUE in the global environment is an error.

arguments.name: enable
arguments.text: If FALSE, return one shared progressor that does nothing.

origin.details: A progressor must be created inside a function, or inside with_progress or without_progress. Each call increments progression_index and signals an update unless type is passed. length(progressor) is the transformed step count. A second progressor in the same frame finishes the previous one first. finalize = TRUE signals type shutdown when the object is collected.

translation.description: Create a callable that signals progression conditions.
translation.usage: progressor(steps=<omitted>, along=None, offset=0, scale=1, transform=None, message=(), label=None, trace=False, initiate=True, finalize=False, auto_finish=True, on_exit=<omitted>, enable=None, envir=None)

arguments.name: steps
arguments.text: Number of steps. When omitted, steps is len(along), and along None is length 0.

arguments.name: transform
arguments.text: Applied once at creation. The default is scale * steps + offset.

arguments.name: initiate
arguments.text: If True, signal type initiate with steps and auto_finish when the progressor is created.

arguments.name: on_exit
arguments.text: If True, signal type finish when the creating frame returns. A frame-return hook does this. True at module level is an error.

arguments.name: enable
arguments.text: If False, return one shared progressor that does nothing. The default option is false when stdin is not a terminal.

translation.details: Calling progressor at module level is the global-environment error unless with_progress or without_progress has allowed it. Inside a function it is allowed. on_exit uses sys.setprofile and signals type finish when that frame returns. finalize=True signals type shutdown from a garbage-collection finalizer, not instead of on_exit. len(progressor) is the transformed step count. A second progressor in the same frame finishes the previous one first.
translation.value: A Progressor. len(progressor) is the transformed steps.
translation.example:
from progressr.condition import condition_message
from progressr.evaluate import with_progress
from progressr.factory import make_progression_handler
from progressr.progressor import progressor

def update(config, state, progression, **kwargs):
    print(progression["type"], f"{progression['amount']:g}", condition_message(progression))

handler = make_progression_handler("rec", reporter={"update": update}, enable=True, target="file", interval=0)

def report():
    progress = progressor(steps=4)
    print(len(progress))
    progress(message="one")
    progress(message="two")
    progress(message="three")
    progress(message="four")

with_progress(report, handlers=handler, enable=True, interval=0, delay_terminal=False, delay_stdout=False, delay_conditions=())
